source.title: Improving generalization of deep fault detection models in the presence of mislabeled data
source.authors: Katharina Rombach; Gabriel Michau; Olga Fink

record.tranche_reason: Tests how symmetric label noise affects clean-test accuracy in fault-detection networks, using a different outcome measure from training error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports clean-test accuracy under symmetric corruption of 0–40% of training labels. It does not report a completely random labeling, zero training error, training time, shuffled or Gaussian inputs, or the real-label/noise learning order. Figure 2 reports training and test accuracy, but its values are figure-only; the text says it demonstrates overfitting to noisy labels.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures part of V4 in binary MNIST and building-fault classification: clean-test performance as symmetric training-label noise increases. Its preliminary ERM experiment also examines noisy-training accuracy, although the supplied figure text does not reveal its values.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that their framework can improve generalization especially under high label noise, with performance depending on dataset, strategy, and the assumed upper noise limit. Under erroneous noise assumptions, baseline mixup is generally less sensitive.
record.recipe_differences: Uses binary fault-detection tasks, symmetric partial label corruption, and clean-test accuracy to evaluate noise-robust training; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, label-noise ratio, method, and whether the assumed upper noise limit matches the actual noise level affect reported accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed outlier-detection and data-modification methods improve clean-test accuracy under some noise conditions; their performance depends on dataset and assumed noise level.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise-aware training can improve generalization under partial label corruption.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man and Cybernetics
record.problems: The experiments use binary classification on MNIST and one building time-series dataset. The paper does not provide tabulated training-error values for the claim's fitting outcome; Figure 2 is not numerically extractable from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the version tested (V4) has tabulated clean-test accuracy outcomes, but those outcomes do not establish the version's required perfect training fit. Figure 2 is described as showing training and test accuracy, but values are figure-only and not recoverable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit real versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training-set fit at each noise level and the trajectory through completely random labeling. Experiments cover only 0–40% label noise; Figure 2's training-accuracy values cannot be read from the supplied text.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting completely random labels, and whether removing them impairs clean-label generalization.
The relative learning order of real-label patterns and noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to correct. The record explicitly declares the omitted Table 3 outcomes and unreadable Figure 2 training values, so they are not additional undeclared missing results. The V4 verdict rests on the supplied table text. The training-accuracy selection threshold of at least 75% is not evidence of perfect fitting or evidence that final accuracy was only 75%.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling or explicit training-error outcome is reported.
Training time and convergence speed by corruption fraction are not reported.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment is reported.
The study reports clean-test accuracy as label noise rises, but does not report perfect training-set fit; the figure's training-accuracy values are not available as text or table values.
Does not test weight decay or dropout, nor whether removing regularization or augmentation harms clean-label generalization.
Does not compare the order in which real-label patterns and noise are learned.

relationships.condition: ERM on binary MNIST and BDD, with 0–40% symmetric label noise; clean-test degradation component only.
relationships.reason: Table 3, rather than extracted rows, shows steadily falling test accuracy: MNIST 99, 91, 82, 72, 62%; BDD 94, 90, 83, 79, 63%. This supports degradation toward binary chance performance, without establishing perfect training fit.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy declined successively to 99%, 91%, 82%, 72%, and 62% on MNIST and 94%, 90%, 83%, 79%, and 63% on BDD.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
